title: Harz and Innsbruck Outdoor Source and Licensing Inventory
legal_notice: This is a technical source-selection inventory, not legal advice. A candidate disposition is not final legal approval. Missing or ambiguous terms are treated as no permission.

pilot_regions.name: Harz pilot
pilot_regions.notes: Bounding box follows the existing outdoor-evidence contract; clip every regional input and retain source provenance.

pilot_regions.name: Innsbruck, Nordkette and bounded Stubai pilot
pilot_regions.notes: Bounding box follows the existing outdoor-evidence contract and includes the intended Innsbruck/Nordkette/Stubai pilot only.

sources.source_name: OpenStreetMap database
sources.provider: OpenStreetMap contributors and OpenStreetMap Foundation
sources.geographical_coverage: Global; clip to both pilot bounding boxes
sources.geometry_availability: Point, line and polygon geometry; relations require assembly and provenance retention.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Element versions/timestamps and replication sequence timestamps are available.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Minutely upstream; project target is a scheduled regional refresh no older than 14 days.
sources.attribution_requirements: Display OpenStreetMap attribution and link to the copyright/license page; retain source and ODbL compliance metadata. Public use of a derivative database may trigger share-alike obligations.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for bulk data.
sources.rate_limits: Bulk/replication hosting limits depend on distributor; do not use the editing API for production reads.
sources.pricing: No data license fee; ingestion, hosting and compliance have operational cost.
sources.privacy_considerations: OSM metadata can identify contributors; do not expose contributor metadata unless needed for license/provenance workflows.
operational_risks: Community-mapped evidence is not an official or real-time ground-truth source.
Missing access is unknown, never allowed.
ODbL derivative-database boundaries need release review.
sources.implementation_notes: Continue the existing fail-closed PostGIS evidence model. Persist source key, OSM identity/version, observed timestamp and import batch. Treat route relations only as mapped route membership, not official designation, unless corroborated by an official source.
unresolved_questions: Confirm the app's exact Produced Work versus Derivative Database boundary before public distribution.

sources.source_name: Geofabrik OpenStreetMap regional extracts
sources.provider: Geofabrik GmbH
sources.geographical_coverage: Germany state extracts and Austria extract
sources.geometry_availability: Same vector geometry as the distributed OSM subset.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Extract timestamps, state files and checksums are published alongside downloads.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Typically daily extracts; verify timestamp before every import.
sources.attribution_requirements: OpenStreetMap/ODbL attribution remains mandatory; Geofabrik requests acknowledgement when its service is used.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for public extract downloads.
sources.rate_limits: No SLA; schedule one regional fetch per refresh and avoid redundant downloads.
sources.pricing: Public downloads are free; commercial support is separately available.
sources.privacy_considerations: Same contributor-metadata considerations as OSM.
operational_risks: Harz requires Niedersachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt and Thüringen extracts and deduplication after clipping.
Distributor availability is not an SLA.
The extract is a delivery channel, not a second claim authority.
sources.implementation_notes: Use as the production acquisition path for OSM, with Niedersachsen/Sachsen-Anhalt/Thüringen unioned and clipped for Harz and Austria clipped for Innsbruck.

sources.source_name: Public OSM tiles, editing API, Nominatim and public Overpass instances
sources.provider: OpenStreetMap Foundation and community instance operators
sources.geographical_coverage: Global services
stable_external_identifiers: OSM element IDs only; service responses and tiles are not durable source records
sources.geometry_availability: Available in responses, but service policies make systematic production acquisition unsuitable.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Varies by service and instance.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Near-real-time in some services, with no product SLA.
sources.attribution_requirements: OSM attribution plus service-specific usage-policy compliance.
sources.authentication_requirements: Varies; identifying User-Agent and contact details are required by several policies.
sources.rate_limits: Nominatim absolute maximum 1 request/second and forbids systematic POI extraction; editing API is not for read-only projects; tile service forbids bulk/offline download; public Overpass has instance-dependent quotas and no SLA.
sources.pricing: Community-funded and free at modest permitted use; this does not imply production entitlement.
sources.privacy_considerations: Queries disclose user interests/locations to third-party services; never send private route prompts or precise user history.
operational_risks: Systematic extraction conflicts with usage policies
Offline tile prefetch is prohibited on the standard tile service
sources.implementation_notes: Use bulk licensed data and self-hosted or contracted infrastructure. A developer-only diagnostic query is not a production dependency.

sources.source_name: Digitales Geländemodell DGM1 Niedersachsen
sources.provider: Landesamt für Geoinformation und Landesvermessung Niedersachsen (LGLN)
sources.geographical_coverage: Lower Saxony portion of Harz
sources.geometry_availability: One-metre elevation raster; derive clipped terrain products.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Product/download metadata and download year; retain selected asset and checksum.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Irregular/cyclic surveying; check catalog monthly, rebuild only on changed assets.
sources.attribution_requirements: Use © GeoBasis-DE/LGLN [download year]; add 'Daten geändert' when modified, under CC BY 4.0.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for open-data endpoints.
sources.rate_limits: No formal API quota found; prefer bulk COG/STAC ingestion and respectful WCS use.
sources.pricing: Free open data.
sources.privacy_considerations: None beyond normal download logs; do not proxy user coordinates to WCS at request time.
operational_risks: Coverage stops at the state boundary.
Vertical datum and CRS must be normalized and recorded.
A terrain model does not establish a traversable or legal route.
sources.implementation_notes: Ingest once, clip to harz-v1, transform to the project's metric CRS, build elevation/slope summaries, and preserve raw asset checksum and attribution year.
unresolved_questions: Verify vertical reference and no-data semantics from the selected asset metadata before implementation.

sources.source_name: Digitales Geländemodell DGM1 Sachsen-Anhalt
sources.provider: Landesamt für Vermessung und Geoinformation Sachsen-Anhalt (LVermGeo ST)
sources.geographical_coverage: Saxony-Anhalt portion of Harz
sources.geometry_availability: One-metre elevation raster; DGM5 is also available as a lighter fallback.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Catalog/service metadata; retain the dataset version and retrieval timestamp.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Cyclic/irregular; poll catalog monthly and rebuild only when version changes.
sources.attribution_requirements: Use © GeoBasis-DE / LVermGeo ST and reference dl-de/by-2-0; mark modifications in accordance with the license.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for open data.
sources.rate_limits: No formal quota found; prefer downloads over per-user WCS traffic.
sources.pricing: Free open data.
sources.privacy_considerations: None beyond normal service logs.
sources.implementation_notes: Use the same raster normalization contract as LGLN; reconcile edge cells but never average away source provenance.
unresolved_questions: Verify the current DGM1 distribution's vertical datum before import.

sources.source_name: Digitale Geländemodelle Thüringen
sources.provider: Thüringer Landesamt für Bodenmanagement und Geoinformation (TLBG)
sources.geographical_coverage: Thuringia portion of Harz
sources.geometry_availability: DGM2/DGM5 raster-like grids; select the best consistent open product for the small pilot overlap.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Product metadata and retrieval date; retain the data-owning office and year.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Cyclic/irregular airborne survey updates; check quarterly.
sources.attribution_requirements: Attribute the data-holding office/GDI-Th, year of retrieval and dl-de/by-2-0; mark modifications.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for open products.
sources.rate_limits: No formal quota found; use bulk delivery.
sources.pricing: Free open data for the listed open products.
sources.privacy_considerations: None beyond ordinary download logs.
operational_risks: Multiple DGM resolutions and delivery styles
Small pilot overlap can hide seam errors
sources.implementation_notes: Select and document one resolution, transform to the same metric/vertical convention as the other Harz models, and preserve source-cell lineage.
unresolved_questions: Confirm which current downloadable DGM product has the clearest version metadata and vertical reference.

sources.source_name: Nationalpark Harz Wegeplan, official trail network and visitor rules
sources.provider: Nationalparkverwaltung Harz
sources.geographical_coverage: Nationalpark Harz only, across Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt
sources.geometry_availability: A mapped network is shown and a plan PDF exists, but no clearly licensed machine-readable feed was located.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: The legal page identifies the plan in force; individual publications have dates.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Low-frequency plan/rule changes; quarterly link check plus legal-change monitoring.
sources.attribution_requirements: No open-data reuse grant was located. Cite and link the Nationalparkverwaltung; do not copy map layers or substantial text without permission.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for public pages; the interactive map can involve third-party services.
sources.rate_limits: Not documented; public webpage only.
sources.pricing: Public viewing is free; reuse rights are not stated.
sources.privacy_considerations: Do not load third-party interactive maps server-side or disclose user route queries.
operational_risks: Plan is legally meaningful but old and may have amendments
Official route status is limited to the park
The website itself warns that field signage controls
sources.implementation_notes: Until written permission or an open feed exists, use only a source link and a fail-closed park-rule gate. If licensed, ingest the authoritative route/allowed-use geometry with plan version and effective date.
unresolved_questions: Can the Nationalparkverwaltung license its route geometry and rule identifiers for commercial app use?
Is a current machine-readable feed available through the new Harz App/Digitize the Planet integration?

sources.source_name: Nationalpark Harz current closures and impairments
sources.provider: Nationalparkverwaltung Harz
sources.geographical_coverage: Nationalpark Harz only
sources.geometry_availability: Map geometry may exist in the presentation layer, but no licensed closure feed is documented; descriptions may be textual.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Page is described as current; individual notices may include dates. Capture observed_at and any explicit start/end date.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Event-driven and live-sensitive; check immediately before route presentation and again before start.
sources.attribution_requirements: No open-data reuse license located; link and attribute the park authority, and do not republish the map/data without permission.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for the page; viewing the map transfers data to ArcGIS according to the page notice.
sources.rate_limits: Not documented; do not scrape.
sources.pricing: Public viewing is free; feed/reuse rights are not stated.
sources.privacy_considerations: Server-side checks should not contain user identifiers or raw prompts; avoid third-party map calls from the client without consent.
operational_risks: Absence of a notice does not prove openness
sources.implementation_notes: For now, deep-link from routes intersecting the park and require the user to review the live official page. Pursue the planned automated interface announced in July 2026.
unresolved_questions: What are the license, schema, completeness and SLA of the planned automated closure interface?
Can closure segment geometry be matched to stable official IDs?

sources.source_name: Harzklub maintained trail network and signage inventory
sources.provider: Harzklub e.V.
sources.geographical_coverage: Harz-wide trail network across all three states
available_formats: internal signage/optimization database of unknown export format
stable_external_identifiers: sign number and UTM coordinate where modernized
sources.geometry_availability: Public pages describe routes; richer geometry/signage data appears to exist internally but is not openly licensed.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Web pages and annual reports conflict on network totals; partner data would need explicit record-level update timestamps.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Maintenance-driven; request at least monthly changes and immediate critical notices in a partnership.
sources.attribution_requirements: The imprint limits copies/downloads to private non-commercial use; written permission is required for commercial reuse.
sources.authentication_requirements: Public pages need none; internal databases likely require a partner account/agreement.
sources.rate_limits: Not applicable until a partner interface is defined.
sources.pricing: Unknown; negotiate data access, support and attribution.
sources.privacy_considerations: Exclude volunteer personal/contact data; ingest only organization-approved trail records.
operational_risks: Conflicting public network totals show stale-content risk
A maintained/marked trail still does not by itself prove legal public access
sources.implementation_notes: Seek a commercial data agreement for route/segment IDs, geometry, signage status, maintenance timestamps and explicit claim scope. Until then, do not scrape or normalize public site content.
unresolved_questions: Does Harzklub expose a partner export/API?
Which organization is authoritative per segment?
Can critical defects/closures be delivered with effective dates?

sources.source_name: Harz official tourism routes and Harzer-Hexen-Stieg notices
sources.provider: Harzer Tourismusverband e.V. (HTV), with Outdooractive technology/content flows
sources.geographical_coverage: Harz tourism region; specific notices vary by route and publisher
sources.geometry_availability: Tour geometry/GPX is offered for some routes; reuse permission is not established by download availability.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Notices may have dates; HTV says closures are shown when known, which is not a completeness guarantee.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Route catalog scheduled; notices live-sensitive and event-driven.
sources.attribution_requirements: No open license for route data was located. The site uses Outdooractive technology/content; commercial archiving or transfer requires the relevant rightsholder's written consent.
sources.authentication_requirements: Public viewing none; partner API requires project/API keys and contract.
sources.rate_limits: Undefined for public pages; contractual for API. Do not scrape.
sources.pricing: Unknown; Outdooractive API/business access is a paid/contractual product.
sources.privacy_considerations: Do not forward user route prompts to embedded third parties; avoid ingesting community comments or profiles.
operational_risks: Downloaded GPX is not a commercial data license
Tourism recommendation is not legal access or current safety
sources.implementation_notes: Prioritize a direct HTV/Nationalpark/Outdooractive agreement that exposes first-party route ownership, closure source, timestamps and content-level license. Link-only until then.
unresolved_questions: Which route objects are owned by HTV versus third parties?
Can TrailMind receive the July 2026 curated Nationalpark routes and future closure interface directly?
What API plan permits server-side normalization and caching?

sources.source_name: Harz official tourism camping and motorhome directory
sources.provider: Harzer Tourismusverband e.V. and listed operators
sources.geographical_coverage: Harz tourism region, broader than the pilot bounding box in places
stable_external_identifiers: tourism directory object ID if supplied
sources.geometry_availability: Point/address presentation; no openly licensed structured geometry feed located.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Page retrieval date only unless an entry exposes its own update timestamp.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Seasonal/irregular; partner feed should be checked weekly in season.
sources.attribution_requirements: No reusable data license located; image licenses shown per asset do not license the directory facts or all media. Obtain written permission before storing or redistributing.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for viewing; unknown for a partner export.
sources.rate_limits: Not documented; do not scrape.
sources.pricing: Public viewing free; data partnership terms unknown.
sources.privacy_considerations: Store organization contact details only when contractually permitted; exclude personal contact data and booking profiles.
operational_risks: An advertised listing does not establish legal approval
The directory may include sites outside the pilot
sources.implementation_notes: Use only as an advertised-place lead until each site is corroborated by an operator or competent authority. Never label an entry 'legal camping' from this directory alone.
unresolved_questions: Is there a licensed HTV accommodation API with persistent IDs and update timestamps?
Which municipal/state source can prove a site's current authorization?

sources.source_name: DELFI national public transport timetable
sources.provider: DELFI e.V. / German federal states and transport authorities
sources.geographical_coverage: Germany-wide scheduled public transport, including Harz trailhead services represented in the feed
sources.geometry_availability: Stop points and optional route shapes; check each feed build for shape completeness.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Feed publication/version and GTFS calendar validity are available; record both retrieval and service validity.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Official metadata indicates weekly delivery; validate feed freshness and calendar coverage before use.
sources.attribution_requirements: CC BY attribution to the named DELFI/provider metadata; preserve provider notices and feed version.
sources.authentication_requirements: Confirm current download endpoint; catalog access itself is public.
sources.rate_limits: Bulk schedule feed; download once per release, not per user request.
sources.pricing: Free under the published license.
sources.privacy_considerations: Static schedules contain no user data; route-search telemetry remains TrailMind data and should be minimized.
operational_risks: Static timetable is not real-time service status
Stop proximity does not prove trail access
Last-mile walking still needs a legal path source
sources.implementation_notes: Build scheduled trailhead reachability only after core evidence. Show timetable validity and an explicit 'check live service' instruction; do not claim a service is currently running from static GTFS.
unresolved_questions: Confirm the current automated download URL and exact required attribution string before implementation.

sources.source_name: Digitales Geländemodell Tirol
sources.provider: Land Tirol, Abteilung Geoinformation (tiris)
sources.geographical_coverage: Tyrol, including Innsbruck/Nordkette/Stubai pilot
sources.geometry_availability: Raster elevation coverage; 5 m is the recommended bounded-pilot product.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: data.gv.at records the updated date (23 May 2025 at research time) and irregular periodicity.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Irregular; poll catalog quarterly and rebuild only on changed distributions.
sources.attribution_requirements: Use 'Datenquelle: Land Tirol - data.tirol.gv.at' under CC BY 4.0 and follow the additional Land Tirol notice requirements, including notifying the authority where the application/service can be found.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for open distributions.
sources.rate_limits: No formal quota located; use bulk downloads.
sources.pricing: Free open data.
sources.privacy_considerations: No need to send user coordinates to the source after precomputation.
operational_risks: Terrain does not prove trail existence, access or condition
sources.implementation_notes: Use 5 m GeoTIFF clipped to innsbruck-v1, transform to the project's metric CRS, retain native CRS/version/checksum, and add the required attribution/notification workflow before release.
unresolved_questions: Confirm the vertical reference and exact notification mechanism with Land Tirol before production launch.

sources.source_name: Graphenintegrations-Plattform GIP Austria OGD export
sources.provider: ÖVDAT and Austrian public-authority GIP partners
sources.geographical_coverage: Austria-wide multimodal public-authority transport graph, clipped to the Tyrol pilot
sources.geometry_availability: Nationwide routable node/edge geometry with mode and infrastructure attributes.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Release version and change history are in each export; site states an approximately two-month refresh cycle.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Approximately every two months.
sources.attribution_requirements: Use 'Datenquelle: gip.gv.at' with gip.gv.at linked, under CC BY 4.0; retain release and originating authority fields.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for OGD download.
sources.rate_limits: Bulk release; download once per release.
sources.pricing: Free open government data.
sources.privacy_considerations: No user data in the static graph; keep route telemetry separate.
operational_risks: Website prose is copyrighted even though the OGD dataset is open
Transport graph permissions may not equal recreational/legal trail access
Release lag can be two months
GIP data is not expert/safety advice
sources.implementation_notes: Pilot as an authoritative transport/access corroboration layer. Map only documented access/restriction semantics, preserve source IDs and release, and keep missing/ambiguous permission fail-closed.
unresolved_questions: Which GIP attributes are sufficiently complete for pedestrian legal-access decisions in Tyrol?
How do hiking-path subnets overlap with the separate official route layer?

sources.source_name: DIGIWAY harmonized official road/trail network and hiking routes
sources.provider: Euregio Tirol-Südtirol-Trentino, Land Tirol and project partners
sources.geographical_coverage: Tyrol, South Tyrol and Trentino; clip Tyrol records to innsbruck-v1
sources.geometry_availability: Line geometry in FC1 transport/path network and FC2 hiking routes.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Daily ETL is documented; retain pipeline run and source-specific timestamps when present.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Daily harmonization of the source OGD.
sources.attribution_requirements: The project states it processes published OGD, but no single explicit license/attribution manifest for the downloadable harmonized packages was located. Resolve and preserve every upstream source license before use.
sources.authentication_requirements: Public downloads/WFS appear unauthenticated.
sources.rate_limits: No documented quota/SLA found; prefer daily bulk package and conditional requests.
sources.pricing: Publicly accessible; license entitlement for commercial reuse is unresolved.
sources.privacy_considerations: No user data expected; do not ingest contact fields unless documented and needed.
operational_risks: Open-access endpoint is not itself a license
Daily ETL does not guarantee daily source changes
Official route membership does not prove current openness
sources.implementation_notes: Technically this is the highest-value Innsbruck route source. Before ingestion, obtain a written license/attribution matrix for the package and verify that Tyrol FC1/FC2 source records are commercially reusable. Then ingest daily with source IDs and classification system retained.
unresolved_questions: What exact license governs the harmonized package and each included source?
Does FC1 contain authoritative pedestrian access restrictions?
Are closures represented and, if so, with effective times and completeness guarantees?

sources.source_name: Tyrol forestry closures / Bergwelt Tirol operational notices
sources.provider: Land Tirol, forest wardens and tourism associations
sources.geographical_coverage: Tyrol; operational coverage depends on participating wardens/DMOs and the cycling-oriented system
stable_external_identifiers: unknown; require closure ID and GIP segment references in a partnership
sources.geometry_availability: Operational geometry exists in radrouting Tirol/Radapp workflows, but no reusable public closure feed was documented.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Warden/DMO entries reportedly include location, reason and duration; API metadata is unknown.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Live/event-driven; must be checked near display/start time.
sources.attribution_requirements: The Land Tirol open-data terms do not automatically license this operational webpage/system. Obtain an explicit feed agreement and attribution from the competent provider.
sources.authentication_requirements: Public viewing varies; feed access unknown.
sources.rate_limits: Unknown until partnership.
sources.pricing: Unknown.
sources.privacy_considerations: Exclude reporter/warden identity and free-text personal data; only ingest authority-approved closure records.
operational_risks: System is described mainly around MTB/forestry use
An expired record can be hazardous
sources.implementation_notes: Request a documented, timestamped closure feed keyed to GIP/DIGIWAY segments. Until available, provide a link in the pre-start checklist rather than asserting open/closed state.
unresolved_questions: Who contracts/licences the operational closure feed?
Is hiking coverage complete in Innsbruck/Nordkette/Stubai?
What are update latency, expiry semantics and service SLA?

sources.source_name: Consolidated Tyrolean Camping Act and official municipal guidance
sources.provider: Austrian Legal Information System (RIS) and Land Tirol
sources.geographical_coverage: Tyrol
sources.geometry_availability: No campsite or exception geometry in the statewide law; municipal ordinance areas must be sourced separately.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: RIS provides consolidation/effective dates; store the exact law version and retrieval date.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Monitor weekly for legal changes and municipal ordinances before any legal claim.
sources.attribution_requirements: Cite the official RIS/Land Tirol source and version. Legal interpretation and translated copy require counsel review; do not imply legal advice.
sources.authentication_requirements: None.
sources.rate_limits: Public legal portal; use periodic link/version checks, not high-rate scraping.
sources.pricing: Free public legal information.
sources.privacy_considerations: None for legislation; municipal case files may contain personal data and are out of scope.
operational_risks: A tourism listing is not proof of authorization
App summaries can become legal advice if overclaimed
No statewide machine-readable registry of approved sites was found
sources.implementation_notes: Use only as a fail-closed rule: do not recommend wild camping. A specific campsite may be labeled authorized only with a current competent-authority or municipal record reviewed by counsel.
unresolved_questions: Where are current municipal exception ordinances published in structured form?
Is there a current registry of lawfully operated campsites and short-stay sites?
What user-facing wording is approved by Austrian counsel?

sources.source_name: Stubai Tourism route catalog and generated hut/alpine-pasture status

sources.rate_limits: Not documented; do not poll or scrape without agreement.
sources.pricing: Unknown.

operational_risks: Tour descriptions may mix tourism copy with facts
A hut opening does not prove beds, water or overnight availability
sources.implementation_notes: Deep-link to the timestamped hut list and individual operator until a feed is licensed. If partnered, store status with observed_at, publisher, operator corroboration and a short expiry; never store 'open' indefinitely.
unresolved_questions: Is there a structured, licensed hut/status API behind the PDF?
Do operators directly maintain their status?
What status TTL and completeness are warranted?
Can route GPX and stats be stored commercially?

sources.source_name: Alpine Clubs hut directory
sources.provider: Österreichischer Alpenverein with DAV/AVS participating hut data
sources.geographical_coverage: Alpine Club huts in Austria, Germany and South Tyrol; relevant Tyrol subset
stable_external_identifiers: hut directory record ID if exposed
sources.geometry_availability: Hut point/map data is displayed; no openly licensed export was located.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Opening/contact data are published, but record-level freshness and operator update timestamps are not guaranteed publicly.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Seasonal and operator-driven; current opening requires near-real-time operator confirmation.
sources.attribution_requirements: The hut disclaimer says all data/text/images/design are copyrighted and use requires express written permission.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for public directory; partner interface unknown.
sources.rate_limits: Not documented; do not scrape.
sources.pricing: Unknown; partnership required.

operational_risks: Directory may link to independently controlled hut pages
Existence/opening do not prove overnight capacity, water, access or safety
sources.implementation_notes: Seek a licensing agreement with stable hut IDs and operator-sourced status timestamps. Until then, use an outbound link and instruct users to contact/book directly.
unresolved_questions: Is a partner API/export available?
Which fields are operator-verified and how often?
Can availability or only scheduled opening be licensed?

sources.source_name: Verkehrsverbund Tirol scheduled timetable via Austria mobility-data platform
sources.provider: Mobilitätsverbünde Österreich OG and Verkehrsverbund Tirol (VVT)
sources.geographical_coverage: Tyrol public transport excluding some national rail content; combine only under compatible agreements
sources.geometry_availability: Stop points and route shapes where supplied.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: National access point lists change-driven updates and annual validity; platform was updated 8 July 2026 at research time.
sources.expected_update_frequency: At change, potentially daily; contractual feed validity and deletions must be enforced.
sources.attribution_requirements: The platform uses a separate free-use license agreement rather than a simple unconditional open license for the VVT feed; comply with provider attribution, validity and termination/deletion clauses after counsel review.
sources.authentication_requirements: Registration and agreement acceptance are required for current platform downloads/API.
sources.rate_limits: Platform/API-specific and account-bound; not stated on the public metadata page.

operational_risks: VVT feed excludes some national rail content
Static schedules are not live operation
sources.implementation_notes: Do not onboard until counsel signs off the current agreement and the deletion/expiry pipeline is designed. Then combine with ÖBB only if both licenses and identifiers are reconciled.
unresolved_questions: What attribution, retention and derived-output terms apply to a commercial route-planning app?
What API quota/SLA applies?
How must expired feed data be deleted from caches and derived products?

sources.source_name: Wikidata entity data
sources.provider: Wikimedia Foundation and Wikidata contributors
sources.geographical_coverage: Global; query only pilot-related entities
sources.geometry_availability: Point coordinates are commonly available; not an authoritative trail-geometry source.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Entity revisions and dump dates; store retrieved revision when material.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Continuously edited; weekly bounded refresh or monthly dump-based crosswalk is sufficient.
sources.attribution_requirements: Structured Wikidata data are CC0; attribution is appreciated but not legally required. Linked external media/data retain their own licenses.
sources.authentication_requirements: None for public read APIs/dumps; follow identifying User-Agent guidance.
sources.rate_limits: Public Query Service and APIs are shared and may throttle; use small bounded queries, caching or dumps rather than runtime dependency.
sources.pricing: Free.
sources.privacy_considerations: Do not ingest contributor/user metadata; entity data may include personal information unrelated to outdoor planning and should be filtered out.
operational_risks: Public query service has no product SLA
sources.implementation_notes: Use only for stable crosswalks, multilingual names and official-site links, with confidence below official/operator sources. Never let a QID upgrade a legal/current claim.

sources.source_name: Wikimedia Commons media and metadata
sources.provider: Wikimedia Foundation and individual media authors
sources.geographical_coverage: Global; media associated with pilot POIs only
sources.geometry_availability: Optional file coordinates; use only to associate media, not as authoritative POI geometry.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: File revision and metadata timestamps are available; licenses can be corrected later, so retain revision and recheck.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Per-asset validation at ingestion and periodic license/takedown audit; no runtime freshness requirement.
sources.attribution_requirements: Per-file license controls. Preserve author, title, license/version, source URL and required notices; comply with share-alike where applicable. Check personality, trademark and other non-copyright rights.
sources.authentication_requirements: API can be unidentified, identified by User-Agent, or authenticated; identified/authenticated access is preferred.
sources.rate_limits: As documented in 2026: unidentified clients are much more constrained; identified/authenticated clients receive higher limits and should use no more than three concurrent requests and honor Retry-After.
sources.pricing: Free subject to each asset's license.
sources.privacy_considerations: Images can show identifiable people, homes or sensitive locations; apply a media privacy/safety review and avoid user-generated EXIF not needed for attribution.
operational_risks: A beautiful photo cannot prove current/scenic route quality
sources.implementation_notes: Build an explicit per-asset allowlist and immutable attribution bundle. Do not ingest arbitrary search results or assume all Commons files share one license.
unresolved_questions: Which license families will the product accept for cropped/derivative thumbnails?
What is the takedown and revalidation cadence?

sources.source_name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
sources.provider: European Union/ESA Copernicus programme; Airbus Defence and Space and DLR source rights
sources.geographical_coverage: Global 30 m surface model; both pilots
sources.geometry_availability: Global 30 m Digital Surface Model raster, not a bare-earth terrain model.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: Static acquisition mainly 2011-2015 with release/tile versions through 2024; retained until 2026 according to collection documentation.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Static; monitor platform/licensing announcements quarterly rather than expecting terrain updates.
sources.attribution_requirements: Use the exact source or modified-product notice required by the GLO-30 license, including DLR, Airbus, Copernicus/EU and ESA wording.
sources.authentication_requirements: Registered Copernicus/CCM user and license acceptance; the GLO-30 view service requires CCM registration from 28 July 2026.
sources.rate_limits: API processing uses account quotas/processing units; bulk S3/OData behavior follows current service documentation.
sources.pricing: Data are free under the license; platform processing quotas and infrastructure may create cost.
sources.privacy_considerations: Use backend bulk ingestion; do not send user route queries/coordinates to CDSE at runtime.
operational_risks: DSM includes vegetation/buildings and can bias route ascent
sources.implementation_notes: Use only as a cross-region fallback or QA baseline where state terrain has gaps. Never blend silently with higher-resolution DTM; record model type, release and attribution.
unresolved_questions: Confirm production account quotas and long-term access after the July 2026 policy change.
Define a QA rule for DSM-versus-DTM ascent divergence.

sources.expected_update_frequency: Not applicable.

sources.source_name: Strava API, activity data and heatmap-derived signals
sources.provider: Strava, Inc. / Strava Ireland Limited and athletes
sources.geographical_coverage: Global user activity platform
stable_external_identifiers: athlete/activity/segment IDs are user/platform data and not suitable evidence keys
sources.geometry_availability: User activity geometry may be available only for the authorizing user and approved purpose.

sources.source_name: Outdooractive Data API and destination partner content
sources.provider: Outdooractive AG and individual content owners/DMOs

sources.geometry_availability: Tour/POI geometry through approved project content.
sources.timestamp_or_update_metadata: API synchronization supports updates; exact fields and deletion semantics depend on project configuration and contract.
sources.expected_update_frequency: Contract/project-specific; synchronize rather than repeatedly full-scan.

unresolved_questions: Can one contract cover HTV, Nationalpark Harz, Innsbruck/Seefeld/Stubai content, or are separate owner grants needed?

Can closures be delivered with authority, validity and geometry guarantees?
What are SLA, rate limits and pricing?

claim_authority_matrix.rule: May say mapped/recorded existence with source and observation timestamp; do not imply current operation, access, safety or legal status.
Use regional DTM first and Copernicus DSM only as labeled fallback/QA; retain model type, resolution, datum, release and uncertainty.
Do not promote an OSM relation to official status without a named authoritative publisher and version.
Missing or ambiguous access is unknown and blocks a positive legal-access claim; field signage and current orders override.
Store valid_from, valid_until, observed_at, affected activity and segment; absence never means open. Live check at display/start.
Preserve the classification system and publisher; never translate difficulty across systems without an explicit mapping and uncertainty.
Treat as planning evidence, not a current guarantee; stale/missing observations stay unknown.
Existence does not imply open, staffed, reservable, safe, accessible or supplied with drinking water.
Require observed_at and short expiry; show source and instruct user to contact/check operator. Scheduled season is not live opening.
Hut existence/opening does not prove a bed or permission; require current operator terms/booking or competent legal record.
Tourism directories and OSM can identify candidates only; never label legal/approved without a current authorization record.
No inventoried source meets the bar. Show unknown and advise carrying/treating water; a spring, hut or tap mapping is not potability/availability proof.
May show mapped existence with provenance; not current flow, access, viewpoint quality or safety.
No inventoried source meets the bar; never infer current flow from existence, season, rainfall forecasts or photographs.
May state mapped/recorded viewpoint existence; do not promise view quality, visibility, access or current openness.
No source can verify scenic quality as fact. Keep 'views/scenic' as requested preference unless a future transparent, evidence-backed model is separately approved.
Only state the specific reported condition with timestamp/scope; never generalize to the whole route or imply safety.
Show schedule validity and distinguish planned from live operation; advise live service verification.
Every asset needs its own author, title, source, license/version, derivative status and non-copyright rights review.
